The vertical lines in the distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM) are considered a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children. This condition is characterized by the presence of fine, linear, or grid-like patterns of inflammation within the esophageal mucosa. These lines can be caused by various factors, including gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), infections, and inflammatory conditions such as eosinophilic esophagitis.

In children, VLEM can be a sign of esophagitis, which is inflammation of the esophagus. Esophagitis can result from a combination of factors, including gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), viral or bacterial infections, and other conditions that cause irritation to the esophageal lining.

The presence of VLEM in children suggests an inflammatory process within the esophagus, which may be indicative of underlying esophagitis. However, it is essential to note that not all cases of VLEM are caused by esophagitis, and further evaluation and diagnostic testing are necessary to determine the underlying cause.

In summary, the presence of vertical lines in the distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM) is considered a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children, suggesting inflammation within the esophagus. A comprehensive evaluation and diagnostic workup are necessary to accurately diagnose and manage this condition.
